messages:
Maya: quick one 11 we need a concise entitlement handshake rule when orgs upgrade so routing, enforcement, and billing all match in reports. product wants zero-surprise behavior for customers.
Jon: clarify scenario: org buys Enterprise but existing keys are still Free/Pro. Do we immediately give those keys Enterprise limits, or preserve key-level entitlements until an admin opts in?
Sarah: finance input: billing should follow what was enforced at request-time. If runtime applied org-level entitlement, invoice lines roll up to org; if key-level, attribute to key but still bill under org bucket. Need deterministic mapping.
Liam: perf constraint: lookup must be constant time on the hot path. no joins to billing or long RPCs. we should use a tiny cached object per key with TTL ~30s.
Anya: product standpoint: expectation is usually immediate uplift after purchase; developers shouldn't be blocked by delayed propagation. we'd like a model where upgrades are applied by default.
Maya: proposed "handshake" (lookup) order that is cache-friendly: 1) admin_pin -> pinned_plan 2) key_explicit -> key_plan 3) org_entitlement -> org_plan 4) system_default -> free. pin is explicit admin action.
Jon: agreed. pin allows staged migration and tests. pin must be visible in Console next to the key.
Liam: routing: resolved_plan drives pool selection. rule: if resolved_plan==enterprise AND key not pinned -> route to enterprise_pool. pinned keys continue to their pinned pool. keep routing decision purely cache-driven.
Maya: burst model: product favors shared credit for Enterprise customers but fairness needs to be maintained. hybrid model suggestion: key-first, then org-borrow with caps.
Jon: hybrid pseudo:

```
allow_request(key, org):
  if key.burst_tokens > 0:
    consume key.burst_tokens
    emit telemetry(source: "key")
    return allow
  if org.allow_borrow and org.burst_tokens > 0 and not org.borrow_cap_exceeded:
    consume org.burst_tokens
    emit telemetry(source: "org", borrowed: "true")
    return allow
  emit telemetry(throttled: "true", reason: "burst_exhausted")
  return throttle
```

Maya: add to that: org.borrow_cap should be configurable by plan (enterprise default unlimited within commitment, pro limited) and have a per-minute window guard.
Sarah: billing nuance: if Pro org borrows beyond committed tokens, mark those borrow events as overage and bill to org; if a key had an explicit key-level entitlement, bill to key. Always tag events with billed_entity.
Liam: implementation detail: atomic borrow operation using Redis Lua to check/decrement key then org to avoid race conditions. cheap and O(1).
Anya: Console UX: show "Effective plan" badge for org, and per-key chips: "inherited", "pinned", "explicit". include a migration CTA: "Apply org plan to keys" that previews changes and supports dry-run.
Maya: rollout plan suggestion: phase 0 read-only surface for effective plan; phase 1 canary enforcement (2-3% traffic) with fail-open semantics; phase 2 gradual ramp.
Jon: fail-open rule: on cache miss or ent lookup error, prefer key_explicit if present else system_default. do not block traffic for entitlement failures. emit a cache_miss metric.
Maya: telemetry fields to add: resolved_plan, enforcement_entity(key|org), billed_entity(key|org), burst_source(key|org), borrowed(true|false), borrow_cap_hit, routing_pool, cache_hit(true|false), cache_ttl_seconds.
Sarah: dashboards: daily borrow_count_by_org, borrow_cost_by_org, throttle_rate_by_plan. product wants a realtime alert if org_borrow_rate > 30% sustained for 10m.
Liam: retention: keep raw borrow events for 90d for billing reconciliation; aggregated rollups 13 months.
Anya: UX acceptance: migration preview shows count of keys affected, pinned exceptions, and a confirm that is idempotent. also include per-key owner/email filter in preview.
Maya: migration API sketch (admin):

```
POST /admin/orgs/{org}/migrations/apply
body: {"target_plan":"enterprise","scope":"all|unowned","dry_run":bool,"preserve_pinned":bool}
resp: {"migration_id":"uuid","preview":{"will_change":int,"pinned":int}}
```

Maya: migration worker should page keys, do conditional writes, and append audit entries. rollback must be supported using audit history.
Jon: note: migration should not retroactively change billing for past requests unless finance requests a reconciliation job. runtime attribution is per-request and authoritative.
Liam: safety: throttle migration worker (default 200 updates/min per org), require 2-click confirmation for >100 keys, and log admin id+IP. also invalidate cache entries on key update.
Sarah: billing action: produce a billing_attr_change event for any key whose enforcement attribution would flip so finance can re-run aggregation if needed.
Maya: action items:
- Jon: RFC w/ cache schema + lookup order + fail-open semantics (due Tue)
- Liam: implement redis cache + Lua borrow script + routing hook + telemetry tags (PR target next Fri)
- Sarah: billing rules doc + invoice examples for borrow/overage (due Thu)
- Anya: UX mocks for chips + migration CTA + preview (design review Wed)
- Maya: dashboard wireframes + alert thresholds (EOW)

Maya: ok, unless anyone objects I'll start the RFC and slot a 30m cross-team sync after Jon's doc. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployed entitlement-cache v2 to canary, health checks green
Maya: thanks all
